data.title: We Think Wasko's (WSE:WAS) Robust Earnings Are Conservative
data.description:
Wasko S.A. (WSE:WAS) recently posted some strong earnings, and the market responded positively. Our analysis found some more factors that we think are good for shareholders.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Wasko's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Wasko recorded an accrual ratio of -0.28. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of zł129m, well over the zł91.9m it reported in profit. Wasko shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

Our Take On Wasko's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, Wasko's accrual ratio indicates strong conversion of profit to free cash flow, which is a positive for the company. And on top of that, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last year. Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. data.title: Earnings Update: KB Components AB (publ) (STO:KBC) Just Reported Its Third-Quarter Results And Analysts Are Updating Their Forecasts
data.description:
It's been a good week for KB Components AB (publ) (STO:KBC) shareholders, because the company has just released its latest quarterly results, and the shares gained 5.4% to kr43.20. KB Components reported in line with analyst predictions, delivering revenues of kr751m and statutory earnings per share of kr1.65, suggesting the business is executing well and in line with its plan. Following the result, the analyst has updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimate suggests is in store for next year.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Following the latest results, KB Components' sole analyst are now forecasting revenues of kr3.33b in 2027. This would be a decent 14% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to jump 260% to kr3.38. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analyst had been anticipated revenues of kr3.34b and earnings per share (EPS) of kr3.39 in 2027. The consensus analyst doesn't seem to have seen anything in these results that would have changed their view on the business, given there's been no major change to their estimates.

View our latest analysis for KB Components

It will come as no surprise then, to learn that the consensus price target is largely unchanged at kr48.00.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. We can infer from the latest estimates that forecasts expect a continuation of KB Components'historical trends, as the 11% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 is roughly in line with the 13% annual growth over the past five years. Compare this with the broader industry, which analyst estimates (in aggregate) suggest will see revenues grow 6.2% annually. So it's pretty clear that KB Components is forecast to grow substantially faster than its industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that there's been no major change in sentiment, with the analyst reconfirming that the business is performing in line with their previous earnings per share estimates. Happily, there were no major changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at kr48.00, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price target.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. At least one analyst has provided forecasts out to 2028, which can be seen for free on our platform here.
